project.name: Hummingbot AI Strategy Router Fork
project.description: An automated crypto-trading platform that normalizes access to centralized and decentralized venues, runs executor-backed strategies, and manages their lifecycle. This fork adds a rule-based AI strategy-routing layer, cross-exchange perpetual funding-rate arbitrage, capital-protection controls, paper-trading observation, and repeatable cloud deployment.

nodes.name: Market Intelligence and Strategy Routing
nodes.summary: This domain turns candles, prices, volume, and active-strategy performance into a classified market regime and a strategy recommendation. It governs a mixed strategy universe while allowing only executor-backed, risk-reviewed candidates to trade and keeping the rest in shadow mode.

businessRules: Insufficient candle history must produce observe mode
Extreme volatility, volume spikes, or active loss must route to protect mode
Only enabled candidates supporting the detected regime may be selected
A recommended strategy different from the active strategy produces a switch decision
crossDomainInteractions: Sends route decisions to Trade Execution and Position Lifecycle
Receives active executor PnL and strategy identity from Risk and Capital Protection
Publishes decision logs and candidate rankings to Operations Monitoring and Deployment

nodes.name: Cross-Exchange Funding Rate Arbitrage
nodes.summary: This domain seeks delta-neutral carry by taking opposite perpetual positions on venues with materially different normalized funding rates. It accounts for entry basis, taker fees, expected exit cost, funding receipts, and the operational risk of one leg failing to open.

businessRules: Funding rates are normalized by each venue's payment interval before comparison
Both legs use equal base amount and opposite sides
Entry requires funding profitability, basis-loss, and net-profitability thresholds
Only one active funding arbitrage per token is allowed
Profit includes executor PnL plus recorded funding payments
crossDomainInteractions: Uses exchange market data and fees through connector abstractions
Creates paired positions through Trade Execution and Position Lifecycle
Uses Risk and Capital Protection to unwind incomplete or failed hedges

nodes.name: Trade Execution and Position Lifecycle
nodes.summary: This domain translates strategy intent into grid and directional executor configurations, places venue orders, and tracks them through fill, barrier, and shutdown states. The executor orchestrator centralizes creation, stopping, storage, performance aggregation, and recovery of positions across controllers.

businessRules: Trading stays disabled unless explicitly enabled in controller configuration
Cooldown and maximum-active-executor limits constrain new actions
Grid routes use maker orders in live connectors and limit orders in paper connectors
Directional positions close on configured stop-loss, take-profit, or time-limit barriers
Stop actions may preserve or flatten the underlying position
crossDomainInteractions: Consumes recommendations from Market Intelligence and Strategy Routing
Reports PnL and executor state to Risk and Capital Protection
Persists order and fill evidence consumed by Operations Monitoring and Deployment

nodes.name: Risk and Capital Protection
nodes.summary: This domain prevents new exposure or exits existing exposure when data quality, volatility, losses, configuration constraints, or multi-leg integrity violate policy. It combines pre-trade route gates with continuous post-trade checks, especially for the asymmetric failure modes of cross-exchange arbitrage.

businessRules: ATR spike, volume spike, or active loss limit triggers protect mode
Short exposure is blocked unless allow_short is enabled
Missing mid-price or active cooldown blocks executor actions
An incomplete or single-leg arbitrage must be unwound after timeout
Stop actions are reissued while any affected executor remains active
crossDomainInteractions: Overrides routing recommendations from Market Intelligence and Strategy Routing
Stops or constrains executors in Trade Execution and Position Lifecycle
Surfaces protect reasons and loss gates to Operations Monitoring and Deployment

nodes.name: Operations Monitoring and Deployment
nodes.summary: This domain makes automated trading observable and promotable by combining log parsing, database inspection, paper PnL estimation, code checks, deployment gates, and cloud runtime management. Its current automation is intentionally paper-first and reports gaps before broader strategy activation or live promotion.

businessRules: Compilation or synthetic-test failure blocks deployment
A missing container, missing fills, or paper loss breach is a high-severity gap
Disabled shadow strategies require adapters before activation
Router code changes must be pinned before promotion
Cloud deployment passes quickstart variables and mounts fork-specific router and executor code
crossDomainInteractions: Observes decisions from Market Intelligence and Strategy Routing
Reconstructs fills and PnL from Trade Execution and Position Lifecycle
Blocks promotion when Risk and Capital Protection reports unsafe state

nodes.name: Classify Market and Route Strategy
nodes.summary: Build technical and execution-state features, classify the current regime, apply risk gates, and recommend the best enabled strategy family.

nodes.name: Govern Strategy Candidate Universe
nodes.summary: Maintain the catalog of live and shadow strategy candidates, map each to supported regimes and execution adapters, and rank candidates for operator review.

nodes.name: Discover Funding Arbitrage Opportunity
nodes.summary: Compare perpetual funding and executable prices across venues to identify the highest expected net carry for each configured token.

nodes.name: Open Delta-Neutral Arbitrage
nodes.summary: Validate profitability and create equal-sized opposing perpetual positions on the selected venue pair.

nodes.name: Supervise and Close Funding Arbitrage
nodes.summary: Track both position legs and funding receipts, then close the pair for achieved profitability, deteriorating funding economics, or executor failure.

nodes.name: Translate Route into Executor Actions
nodes.summary: Turn a switch, protect, or stop decision into grid creation, directional position creation, or executor stop actions.

nodes.name: Execute Position Lifecycle
nodes.summary: Create executor instances, validate and place orders, monitor fills and barriers, close exposure, and persist execution outcomes.

nodes.name: Gate Market and Configuration Risk
nodes.summary: Block or reduce trading when input data, market stress, active loss, short permissions, or execution readiness violate configured policy.

nodes.name: Recover Unbalanced Arbitrage
nodes.summary: Detect incomplete, failed, or single-leg arbitrage entries and repeatedly stop remaining exposure until the pair is safely resolved.

nodes.name: Monitor Paper Trading Runtime
nodes.summary: Combine router logs, event logs, SQLite orders and fills, and container health into a human-readable paper-trading report.

nodes.name: Run Paper Iteration and Promotion Gates
nodes.summary: Test router code, inspect live paper evidence, identify prioritized gaps, optionally redeploy paper trading, and verify the resulting runtime.

nodes.name: Deploy Cloud Trading Runtime
nodes.summary: Synchronize the fork and its configuration to a cloud host, pass quickstart settings, mount fork-specific modules, and operate Hummingbot as a managed container.

nodes.name: Load Candles and Mid Price
nodes.summary: Read the configured candle window and current mid price while resolving paper connectors to their base market-data connector.

nodes.name: Build Market Features
nodes.summary: Compute ATR, Bollinger width, EMA trend and slope, volume z-score, completed-range boundaries, and active executor PnL.

nodes.name: Apply Extreme Risk Gate
nodes.summary: Return protect mode immediately when loss, ATR, or volume thresholds indicate unacceptable risk.

nodes.name: Detect Market Regime
nodes.summary: Classify breakouts, directional trends, and low- or high-volatility ranges from the generated features.

nodes.name: Select Route Action
nodes.summary: Choose the highest-priority enabled candidate and decide whether to continue, switch, or protect relative to the active strategy.

nodes.name: Publish Decision and Rankings
nodes.summary: Store features, decision, candidate scores, and registry state for action generation, status output, and monitoring.

nodes.name: Register Strategy Families
nodes.summary: Catalog grid, trend, mean-reversion, market-making, arbitrage, hedge, LP, protect, and observation candidates.

nodes.name: Declare Regime Coverage
nodes.summary: Associate each candidate with the market regimes where its business logic is intended to operate.

nodes.name: Hold Unadapted Candidates in Shadow
nodes.summary: Disable candidates lacking feature, signal, allocation, inventory, or risk adapters while retaining them for scoring and roadmap visibility.

nodes.name: Rank Candidates
nodes.summary: Score candidates by regime support, confidence, priority, enablement, and protect fallback semantics.

nodes.name: Collect Venue Funding
nodes.summary: Retrieve current perpetual funding information for each token from every configured connector.

nodes.name: Normalize Payment Intervals
nodes.summary: Convert venue-specific one-hour or eight-hour funding rates into a common per-second basis and daily profitability horizon.

nodes.name: Choose Long and Short Venues
nodes.summary: Select the connector pair with the largest absolute normalized funding difference and orient the cheaper funding side long.

nodes.name: Estimate Entry Economics
nodes.summary: Use quote-volume prices and taker fee schedules to estimate basis, slippage, and fee profitability for both market-entry legs.

nodes.name: Calculate Net Carry
nodes.summary: Combine funding profitability with entry economics and subtract the configured exit-cost buffer to form the candidate net profitability.

nodes.name: Skip Active Token
nodes.summary: Evaluate a token only when it has no currently active funding arbitrage record.

nodes.name: Apply Profitability Thresholds
nodes.summary: Require minimum funding carry, cap acceptable entry loss, require minimum net profitability, and optionally require nonnegative entry profitability.

nodes.name: Size Equal Opposite Legs
nodes.summary: Derive one base amount from the smaller quote-normalized venue capacity so both legs carry equal and opposite token exposure.

nodes.name: Record Opening Arbitrage
nodes.summary: Persist connector pair, executor IDs, side, economics, timestamps, funding payments, and opening status for supervision.

nodes.name: Create Both Position Executors
nodes.summary: Emit two market-entry executor actions, one long and one short, for the selected perpetual venues.

nodes.name: Collect Matching Executors
nodes.summary: Resolve the executor records belonging to each active arbitrage using the stored pair of executor IDs.

nodes.name: Record Funding Payments
nodes.summary: Append completed funding-payment events to the active arbitrage associated with the event token.

nodes.name: Aggregate Total PnL
nodes.summary: Combine both executors' net trading PnL with accumulated funding cash flows.

nodes.name: Recheck Funding Edge
nodes.summary: Recompute the directionally relevant normalized funding difference while the arbitrage remains open.

nodes.name: Trigger Pair Exit
nodes.summary: Stop both legs when total profitability exceeds target or when the funding spread crosses the configured stop-loss threshold.

nodes.name: Archive Completed Arbitrage
nodes.summary: Capture final trading and funding PnL, move the record to stopped history, and release the token for a later opportunity.

nodes.name: Enforce Trading Enable and Readiness
nodes.summary: Return no actions unless trading is explicitly enabled and a current mid price is available.

nodes.name: Enforce Cooldown and Capacity
nodes.summary: Suppress rapid route churn and limit strategy creation to the configured maximum number of active executors.

nodes.name: Stop for Protect or Switch
nodes.summary: Emit stop actions for active executors when protection is required or the selected strategy must change.

nodes.name: Create Grid Executor Config
nodes.summary: Build a scaled price band, order sizing, maker policy, and grid take-profit configuration for range regimes.

nodes.name: Create Trend Position Config
nodes.summary: Build a scaled long or short market position with leverage, stop loss, take profit, and time limit for trend regimes.

nodes.name: Dispatch Executor Action
nodes.summary: Route create, stop, and store actions through the central executor orchestrator.

nodes.name: Instantiate Executor
nodes.summary: Instantiate the executor type encoded by the controller configuration and register it under the controller.

nodes.name: Validate and Place Open Order
nodes.summary: Validate account balance and activation bounds, then submit the configured opening order through the connector.

nodes.name: Monitor Position Barriers
nodes.summary: Continuously evaluate stop loss, trailing stop, take profit, and time limit after sufficient fill volume is established.

nodes.name: Flatten and Shut Down
nodes.summary: Cancel remaining opening orders, submit the opposite market close for residual size, and transition the executor to shutdown.

nodes.name: Persist Outcome and Performance
nodes.summary: Store completed executor state, update cached positions, and expose controller-level performance reports.

nodes.name: Wait for Sufficient Data
nodes.summary: Remain in observe mode with zero position scale until the largest required indicator window is available.

nodes.name: Detect Market Stress and Loss
nodes.summary: Flag active loss, ATR spike, and volume spike reasons against configurable thresholds.

nodes.name: Route to Protect Mode
nodes.summary: Recommend zero new exposure and a protect action before considering any regime-specific strategy.

nodes.name: Block Unapproved Shorts
nodes.summary: Replace a trend-short recommendation with observe or protect semantics unless shorting was explicitly enabled.

nodes.name: Stop Active Executors
nodes.summary: Issue stop actions for all active controller executors, optionally retaining the resulting position only when protection policy requests it.

nodes.name: Reconcile Expected Legs
nodes.summary: Compare stored executor IDs with observed executor records and their active, trading, done, and failure states.

nodes.name: Allow Bounded Entry Window
nodes.summary: Permit both position executors a configured number of seconds to appear and begin trading before declaring imbalance.

nodes.name: Classify Entry Failure
nodes.summary: Distinguish missing executors, executor failures, one trading leg, and a total entry timeout to preserve an actionable stop reason.

nodes.name: Reissue Idempotent Stop Actions
nodes.summary: Continue issuing stop actions for any active leg while the arbitrage is in stopping state so transient processing failures do not leave exposure open.

nodes.name: Archive Incomplete Resolution
nodes.summary: Close and archive an incomplete arbitrage once all known executors are done, even when fewer than the expected two legs were created.

nodes.name: Read Router Decisions
nodes.summary: Parse structured regime, action, active strategy, recommendation, confidence, scale, and reason fields from router logs.

nodes.name: Read Fill Events
nodes.summary: Parse order-filled event JSON and normalize side, price, amount, fees, order IDs, and trade IDs.

nodes.name: Inspect Order Database
nodes.summary: Query SQLite for order and fill counts, status distributions, and the most recent orders.

nodes.name: Estimate Mark-to-Market PnL
nodes.summary: Reconstruct base inventory, quote cash, fees, buy and sell notionals, and marked equity from parsed fills.

nodes.name: Check Container Health
nodes.summary: Inspect Docker status for the named paper-trading container.

nodes.name: Render Operator Report
nodes.summary: Assemble the latest decision, protect state, order evidence, fills, PnL, and container health into an operator-facing report.

nodes.name: Compile Router Code
nodes.summary: Compile the controller, router modules, monitor, iteration loop, and patched executor files before any deployment decision.

nodes.name: Run Synthetic Regime Tests
nodes.summary: Exercise unknown, range, uptrend, downtrend, and extreme-volume cases and verify their expected route decisions.

nodes.name: Snapshot Live Evidence
nodes.summary: Capture paper container, order, fill, status, decision, configuration, and PnL state from logs and SQLite.

nodes.name: Evaluate Operational Gaps
nodes.summary: Classify code, deployment, execution, risk, configuration, adapter, and release gaps by severity with recommended actions.

nodes.name: Optionally Deploy Paper
nodes.summary: Replace the paper container only after prerequisites pass, mounting the local router and executor implementation into the official image.

nodes.name: Verify Post-Deploy Runtime
nodes.summary: Reinspect the restarted container and report whether paper operation remains healthy after promotion.

nodes.name: Acquire Deployment Lock
nodes.summary: Serialize deployments on the shared cloud host to avoid overlapping release mutations.

nodes.name: Synchronize Project
nodes.summary: Rsync source, controller, router, executor, and non-secret configuration structure while preserving remote runtime data and connector secrets.

nodes.name: Write Runtime Environment
nodes.summary: Generate the remote Compose environment carrying quickstart password, strategy config, headless mode, and image selections.

nodes.name: Mount Fork-Specific Code
nodes.summary: Mount router modules and modified executor implementations over the base Hummingbot image alongside controllers, scripts, logs, data, and certificates.

nodes.name: Start and Operate Cloud Services
nodes.summary: Start or update Hummingbot and optional Gateway services, then expose only the host health endpoint through Nginx while retaining CLI-oriented bot operation.

edges.description: Route decisions become grid, trend, stop, or protect executor actions.
Regime decisions are overridden by stress, loss, and configuration gates.
Profitable funding candidates create two opposing position executors.
Paired positions are supervised for missing legs, failures, timeouts, and deteriorating carry.
Protection policy blocks creation and stops or flattens active executors.
Orders, fills, statuses, and PnL are persisted and consumed by paper monitoring.
Decision logs, candidate scores, and route state feed reports and promotion gates.
Protect mode, paper-loss gates, and short constraints block unsafe promotion.
